evidence: Reviewed unified diffs for all 6 manifest paths (openspec/changes/tui-self-update-offer/tasks.md, tui/main_test.go, tui/model.go, tui/run.go, tui/view.go, tui/view_test.go) for security, authorization, data exposure, unsafe input handling, secrets, and dependency-vulnerability risk.

In tui/run.go, probeBehindOriginCmd builds exec.Command(bin, "sync-check") with a hardcoded literal argument and no shell interpolation (Go's os/exec never invokes a shell), so no command-injection vector is introduced by this candidate; root is not attacker-supplied request data, and cmd.CombinedOutput()'s failure path degrades safely to RepoBehindOriginNA.

In tui/view.go, repoLine renders m.behindOrigin through fmt.Sprintf's %d verb (an int field, not attacker-controlled free text used as a format string), and no secrets, credentials, tokens, or newly introduced external dependency versions appear anywhere in the 6 changed files (no go.mod/go.sum entries are in the manifest).
openspec/changes/tui-self-update-offer/tasks.md only toggles existing checkbox markers from [ ] to [x]; no manifest, dependency, or configuration content changed.

findings.claim: probeBehindOriginCmd runs bin/labdrian-overlay sync-check via exec.Command with no context deadline, timeout, or cancellation, and discards CombinedOutput's error. tui/model.go:86 now wires this into Init() (previously return nil), so every TUI launch spawns this unbounded subprocess call; a slow-to-exit or hung backend leaves the probe goroutine blocked indefinitely with no diagnostic signal, and since bubbletea does not cancel outstanding tea.Cmd goroutines on tea.Quit, the child process can keep running after the user quits the TUI.
proof_refs: tui/run.go:292 cmd := exec.Command(bin, "sync-check") sets no context.WithTimeout/CommandContext and no cmd.Cancel/WaitDelay.

tui/model.go:86 func (m model) Init() tea.Cmd { return probeBehindOriginCmd(m.repoRoot) } replaces the prior return nil, so this unbounded subprocess call now runs unconditionally on every TUI launch.
tui/run.go:294 discards the CombinedOutput error via out, _ :=, so a failed-to-start or hung backend is indistinguishable from a healthy zero-verdict probe.
